title: RBI Dollar-Rupee Swap Draws $72.85 Billion as NRI Deposit Window Closes Monday
excerpt: The FCNR-B deposit scheme, which raised $65.4 billion in 75 days, has been closed early due to overwhelming demand. NRIs have until August 31 to lock in 6-7.5% returns on dollar deposits.
body:
• The RBI's special USD-INR forex swap facility has drawn $72.85 billion as of August 21, with FCNR-B deposits accounting for $65.4 billion raised in just 75 days.
  • The central bank advanced the FCNR-B closure from September 30 to August 31 due to overwhelming response, giving NRIs until Monday to participate.
  • Banks raised $13.1 billion in the last week alone, with NRIs earning 6-7.5% returns on 3-5 year dollar deposits.
  • The scheme has already surpassed the 2013 FCNR-B program, which raised $26 billion over three months. Nomura estimates the total could reach $80 billion by the deadline.

$72.85 Billion and Counting

The Reserve Bank of India's special dollar-rupee forex swap facility, launched on June 8, has attracted $72.85 billion in total inflows as of August 21, according to central bank data. Of that, $65.4 billion came through the FCNR-B (Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank) deposit route — a sum mobilized in just 75 days that far exceeds the RBI's original expectations.

The response prompted the RBI to advance the FCNR-B window's closure from September 30 to August 31, a decision announced on August 14. NRI depositors now have until Monday to lock in deposits.

Banks also raised an additional $4.86 billion through the Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowing (OFCB) route, which remains open through December 31.

A Surge in the Final Stretch

Inflows accelerated sharply as the revised deadline approached. Banks mobilized $13.1 billion in the week of August 13-21 alone, compared to $15.6 billion over the preceding 13 days. The acceleration reflects a rush by NRI depositors and banks scrambling to capture remaining demand before the window shuts.

Indian banks have been offering NRIs returns of 6-7.5% on 3-5 year FCNR-B deposits, rates that compare favorably to declining yields on U.S. dollar savings products. Some banks have extended leverage facilities to NRI customers to maximize deposit volumes, further fueling inflows.

Nomura estimates the total could reach $80 billion by the August 31 deadline. Including ECB and OFCB flows, which remain open through year-end, the broader program could eventually draw $90-100 billion.

Dwarfing the 2013 Precedent

The current scheme has comfortably surpassed the RBI's 2013 FCNR-B program, widely regarded as one of India's most successful forex interventions. That scheme raised $26 billion over three months during a period when the rupee was under severe pressure and India's current account deficit had ballooned.

The 2026 program was launched under different circumstances — the rupee has been more stable — but the scale of response has nonetheless surprised policymakers and economists.

SBI's chief economist said the scheme's target has likely already been achieved. The Indian government characterized the response as reflecting "strong confidence of the Indian diaspora in the Indian banking system."

What It Means for the Rupee and NRI Depositors

For the rupee, the massive dollar inflows provide a substantial buffer against depreciation pressure. The FCNR-B deposits represent committed dollar capital that stays in the banking system for 3-5 years, giving the RBI more flexibility in managing the exchange rate.

For NRI depositors, the window represents a time-limited opportunity. The 6-7.5% returns on dollar-denominated deposits carry no currency risk for the depositor since both the principal and interest are paid in foreign currency. At current rates, the yields exceed most comparable dollar-denominated fixed-income products available in the United States.

The FCNR-B window closes Monday. NRIs considering participation should contact their Indian bank before the August 31 cutoff. The OFCB route remains available for banks seeking to raise additional foreign currency borrowings through year-end.
nri_angle: The FCNR-B scheme directly impacts NRI depositors who can lock in 6-7.5% returns on dollar-denominated deposits with Indian banks, with the window closing August 31.
